cf.title: LLVM JIT: any JIT-compiled query crashes (SIGILL) on a libLLVM 19 + ASAN build

input.subject: LLVM JIT: any JIT-compiled query crashes (SIGILL) on a libLLVM 19 + ASAN build

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection stops the proposal at level 1a or 1b: the crash is reproducible, CI demand is shown, and a committer pushed 0004 as 0607aa61090. The one surviving objection, maintenance-fit-2, is a fixable level 2 point about whether a source pragma or filtering instrumentation flags from the bitcode flags is the better long-term fix. What remains (0002, the jit test, the build-system approach) is for a committer who knows the JIT build to decide.

brief.title: Fix LLVM JIT crash on AddressSanitizer builds and add a jit test
brief.problem: On a build with -fsanitize=address, every JIT-compiled query crashes or hangs the backend, even SELECT 1. Linux backends die of SIGILL or SIGSEGV inside LLVM debug-info code, and macOS loops forever inside LLVM. The regression tests miss it because jit is off by default, and the crash breaks the CI AddressSanitizer job for other patches.
brief.proposed_design: AddressSanitizer wraps each global variable in llvmjit_types.c in an unnamed struct { T, [N x i8] }, so llvm_pg_var_type() hands the JIT a wrong type and the JIT builds invalid IR. v4 makes llvm_pg_var_type() raise an error for an unnamed struct type, and either takes T out of the wrapper (0003) or excludes the file's variables from instrumentation with a clang pragma (0004). It also adds a jit regression test.
user_visible_surface: New regression test jit (sql/jit.sql, expected/jit.out) in parallel_schedule; it sets jit = on and jit_above_cost = 0.
New error: "variable TypeSizeT in llvmjit_types.c is not of its declared type" for a JIT type variable of an unexpected form.
Earlier versions (v2, v3) added a meson warning() and a configure warning when sanitizer flags are filtered from bitcode flags; v4 drops these.
author_claims: The crash reproduces on plain master with a trivial query and is not specific to the Row Pattern Recognition patch.
It reproduces on LLVM 19, 20 and 21, on x86_64 and arm64, on Linux and macOS.
With 0002 the crash becomes an ERROR; with 0003 or 0004 the jit test passes, and Greg Burd confirmed this on Debian 13 and aarch64.
0003 depends on the internal shape of the AddressSanitizer wrapper; 0004 does not but adds a clang-specific pragma.
Committing the test alone breaks the CI AddressSanitizer build.
brief.thread_state: Andres Freund pushed 0004 to 17 through master as 0607aa61090, and Greg Burd and Matheus Alcantara reviewed earlier versions. Open items: 0002, 0003, the test, backpatching to older branches, and a possible build-system approach (filtering c_args or replacing 1039352e1); the CommitFest entry still shows Needs review and needs a rebase.
unclear: The material does not say whether 0002 and the jit test are still wanted after 0004 was committed, or what the next version will contain.
The material does not say whether the -g change for autoconf BITCODE_CFLAGS from v2/v3 is still proposed.
The material does not say how long the jit test runs or whether it runs on builds without LLVM.
The material does not say if other sanitizers, such as UBSan, cause similar problems in the JIT bitcode.

objections.title: Per-sanitizer source pragmas may not scale to other instrumentation
objections.failure_scenario: A developer builds with another sanitizer that also changes global types in llvmjit_types.c, such as hwaddress. The 0004 pragma does not cover that sanitizer, so JIT queries fail again, and the developer finds out only when a JIT test runs. Each new sanitizer would then need its own pragma or unwrapping rule.
objections.argument: The root cause is that 1039352e1 passes all c_args, including instrumentation flags, into bitcode compilation (message #10). 0002 and 0004 address one effect of one sanitizer at the point where types are read. Message #10 names filtering c_args, or replacing 1039352e1, as possible alternatives, and v2/v3 (messages #5, #7) already did this filtering. The material does not show whether UBSan or other sanitizers cause similar breakage.
objections.author_must_show: Does any sanitizer besides AddressSanitizer change the types in llvmjit_types.c bitcode, and if so, why is a source pragma better than filtering instrumentation flags out of bitcode_cflags?

critic.reasoning: Message #10 leaves open the choice between the pragma and filtering c_args, and the thread does not say whether other sanitizers change these types. The hwaddress case is unverified, so this stands as a question for the next version.

refuted.title: 0003 would add unreachable code tied to AddressSanitizer internals
refuted.failure_scenario: With 0004 committed, no supported build reaches the redzone-unwrapping code in 0003. A later clang release changes the wrapper shape and nobody notices, because no build exercises that branch. If 0004 is ever reverted, an untested fallback becomes the only path.
refuted.argument: Message #8 says 0003 relies on the { T, [N x i8] } shape and is never reached when 0004 is applied. Message #9 prefers 0004, and message #10 shows 0004 is committed to 17 through master. Keeping 0003 as well means carrying code that depends on a sanitizer's private layout but never runs in CI.
refuted.author_must_show: Now that 0004 is committed, which supported build would still reach the 0003 code, and how would CI catch it if that code breaks?

critic.reasoning: Message #8 offers 0003 and 0004 as alternatives and says only one is needed. Andres Freund picked 0004 in message #10, and nothing in the thread proposes keeping 0003 as well.

refuted.title: 0003 duplicates the fix already committed as 0004
refuted.failure_scenario: 0607aa61090 already keeps the llvmjit_types.c variables from being wrapped on 17 through master, so the code added by 0003 is never reached there. Years later, a change in the AddressSanitizer wrapper shape, or a change to llvm_pg_var_type(), can break that branch. No test would notice, because no supported build exercises it.
refuted.argument: Message #8 says only one of 0003 and 0004 is needed, and that with both applied the 0003 code "is just not reached". Message #10 pushes 0004, and message #9 leans towards 0004 because it does not depend on AddressSanitizer internals. Adding 0003 now would give a second mechanism for a solved case, and that mechanism depends on an undocumented sanitizer layout. Branches before 17 do not need either fix, by message #10.
refuted.author_must_show: Which supported branch or compiler still wraps the llvmjit_types.c variables after 0607aa61090, so that 0003 would be reached?

critic.reasoning: Same point as maintenance-fit-1. Message #8 presents 0003 only as an alternative to 0004, and the commit of 0004 in message #10 settles that choice without anyone asking for both.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The entry targets stable branches; 0004 went to 17 through master, and backpatching of the remaining pieces is open.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: A clang-specific pragma in llvmjit_types.c, a new check in llvm_pg_var_type(), and a new jit regression test need upkeep.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: After 0607aa61090, what will the next version contain: 0002, the jit test, both, or a build-system change instead?
Does any sanitizer besides AddressSanitizer, such as UBSan, change the variable types in the llvmjit_types.c bitcode?
Why is the source pragma preferable to filtering instrumentation flags out of the bitcode flags, as v2 and v3 did?
How long does the jit test run, and what does it do on a build without LLVM?
Is the -g change for autoconf BITCODE_CFLAGS from v2 and v3 still proposed?

committability.owner_note: Andres Freund pushed 0004 as 0607aa61090; the rest needs someone who knows the LLVM JIT provider and the bitcode build flags in meson and autoconf.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a jit test that must stay stable across LLVM versions and build configurations on every backpatched branch, and for an error check tied to how compilers shape the type variables.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted four versions and moved the entry through three CommitFests; the entry needs a rebase since 2026-11-09 and no later version is visible.

priority.reason: The patches are small and touch only the JIT provider and the regression schedule, and the main fix is already committed. The benefit goes to developers and CI runs that use sanitizer builds, and the entry needs a rebased version that states what is still proposed.

provisional_note: Without the code, the review cannot judge whether the 0002 check rejects any valid non-sanitizer type, or whether the jit test output is stable on builds without LLVM. Only 3 of 11 messages were read in full.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Enable jitlink as an alternative jit linker of legacy Rtdyld and add riscv jitting support
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the LLVM JIT provider use JITLink (ObjectLinkingLayer) in place of RuntimeDyld, through a new C++ wrapper because LLVM has no C API for it. It turns this on for riscv with LLVM 15 or later and hard-codes riscv ABI names, CPU features, PIC relocation and the medium code model.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund said the riscv ABI and target machine settings belong in LLVM, and that the missing JITLink C API should be proposed to LLVM. Thomas Munro asked why JITLink was used only for riscv and why riscv needed manual feature and ABI selection. The author agreed to try the LLVM patches later and asked to keep the workarounds meanwhile. No reviewer replied after that, and no new patch version appears.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think this is something that should go into the llvm code, rather than
postgres.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add llvm version into the version string
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the LLVM version to PG_VERSION_STR, the way the gcc version is already shown, so that JIT bug reports include it. A later version takes the runtime version from the loaded library through LLVMGetVersion, an API that exists from LLVM 16 on.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the configure-time llvm-config version may not match the library loaded at run time. He also objected that changing what version() returns can break code that parses it, and that adding subsystem versions to it does not scale to ICU or libxml2. He suggested a new system view instead, the author agreed to try that direction, and others proposed showing both build-time and runtime versions in the view.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Adding rows to a view over time seems way less likely to cause
problems than messing with a string people probably have crufty
parsing code for.

precedents_retrieved.title: plpgsql - possibility to get element or array type for referenced variable type
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets PL/pgSQL `%TYPE` refer to variables of composite type, including polymorphic parameters. It also adds syntax to derive the array type or the element type of a referenced variable, first as `%ARRAYTYPE`/`%ELEMENTTYPE` and later as `%TYPE[]` and `ELEMENT OF ...%TYPE`.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane proposed rejecting this PL/pgSQL-only implementation. He wanted these type operators added to the core grammar's Typename production, so PL/pgSQL would pick them up automatically. Joe Conway and Jim Nasby agreed. The author then found that a reduced patch with only the composite `%TYPE` fix gave too little benefit, and asked for it to be rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I played with the reduced patch, and the benefit without all other things
is negligible. It should be rejected.

precedents_retrieved.title: Propagate sanity checks of ProcessUtility() to standard_ProcessUtility()?
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves the argument sanity checks that ProcessUtility() runs into a macro and also runs them in standard_ProcessUtility(). The goal is to catch extensions that pass bad arguments, such as a NULL query string, down a chain of utility hooks.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas judged that the change saves little debugging time, since a hook that passes bad arguments crashes quickly and a backtrace shows the cause. He also preferred to keep the assertions visible in place of a macro, and noted that such superficial checks would not catch errors in hooks that change the node tree. Michael Paquier did not argue further and the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I can't imagine a scenario where this change saves more than 5 minutes
of debugging, so I'd rather leave things the way they are.

precedents_retrieved.title: psql \setfileref - new psql variable type - reference to file
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a new psql meta-command, \setfileref, that creates a file-reference variable whose content is read from the named file when the variable is interpolated into a query. This would let users insert large text or binary data (as bytea by default) without manual escaping or the large-object API, with the values sent as query parameters instead of being inlined into the query text.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected to tying the behaviour to a new typed kind of psql variable with one-off syntax, and to psql silently switching to parameterized queries. He suggested a colon-based syntax and a separate setting for parameterized queries instead. The author then dropped \setfileref for a curly-brace 'content commands' syntax, which Robert Haas criticised as a new escaping and interpolation system unrelated to the existing one, and then posted separate patches following Daniel Verite's backtick-based proposal and a variable to enable parameterized queries. The last visible message moves the reworked patches to the next commitfest because no reviewer had responded; the visible messages do not show why the entry was finally returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I really dislike the notion of keying the behavior to a special type of
psql variable.

precedents_retrieved.title: Make PostgreSQL sanitizers-friendly (and prevent information disclosure)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch zeroes memory that MemorySanitizer reports as uninitialized, such as padding bytes in structs written to WAL and data files, and in one version zeroes all memory returned by palloc in aset.c. The goal was to make Postgres pass clang sanitizer checks and to stop leftover stack data from reaching disk.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas marked it returned with feedback because the patch needed more work. He objected that zeroing all palloc'd memory goes too far, costs performance and can hide real bugs, and he asked why several hunks were needed at all. Tom Lane rejected the security argument and suggested sanitizer users should adapt the existing valgrind suppression rules instead of adding runtime zeroing.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think this goes too far. You're zeroing all palloc'd memory, even if
it's going to be passed to palloc0(), and zeroed there.

precedents_retrieved.title: Increasing regression test coverage based on GCOV analysis
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds regression tests chosen from GCOV coverage reports, starting with float8-to-float4 overflow and underflow errors in float.h and a descending sort on numeric for abbreviated-key sorting in sortsupport.h. The author planned to repeat this for other untested code, one area at a time.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The two replies welcomed the work and asked for a commitfest entry, which the author then created, and no objection appears.

precedents_retrieved.title: audo-detect and use -moutline-atomics compilation flag for aarch64
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make configure detect gcc's -moutline-atomics flag and add it to CFLAGS on aarch64. The flag makes the compiler choose at run time between LSE atomic instructions and load-exclusive/store-exclusive sequences, depending on what the CPU supports.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas rejected it because the choice to enable -moutline-atomics belongs to the compiler or the distribution, and Postgres should not override their defaults. Tom Lane had asked earlier whether enough production systems use a gcc with this flag but without it on by default to justify a configure check. The author's benchmarks showed only modest gains, about 6% on pgbench simple-update.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If it's a good idea to use -moutline-atomics, I would expect the
compiler or distribution to enable it by default.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Remove reset of testtablespace from pg_regress on Windows"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Remove reset of testtablespace from pg_regress on Windows"
Reverted commit(s): Remove reset of testtablespace from pg_regress on Windows; Lower privilege level of programs calling regression_main
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 2b2a070, that moved the reset of path
"testtablespace" used by the regression tests as a path for tablespaces
(via --outputdir) from pg_regress to the MSVC script vcregress.pl, as
this broke the behavior added by ce5d342 to be able to safely run the
regression test suite with an administrative Windows account using a
restricted token.

Note that before 2b2a070, the code doing the reset in pg_regress.c
included a comment telling that we had better move that out to a
different place, leading to the mistake done in 2b2a070.  Fix this
comment, and document instead that we had better never remove this code,
for the sake of not breaking again the behavior we expect on Windows.

Thanks to Thomas Munro and Andrew Dunstan for the discussion.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P6] and [P1] are in neighbouring areas but are different ideas, and their recorded reasons do not apply here. [P6] objected to zeroing all palloc'd memory at runtime, and this proposal adds no runtime cost to normal builds. [P1] asked for target-specific settings to live in LLVM, but the AddressSanitizer wrapper is valid compiler output and the faulty assumption sits in llvm_pg_var_type(). The thread cites only one earlier change, 1039352e1 in message #10, which added c_args to the bitcode flags; nobody describes an earlier proposal of this fix.

The proposal adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object, psql feature or dump state, and no existing user behaviour changes; 0004 is already committed. What remains is a regression test and an internal error for a malformed JIT type, neither of which touches the user-facing contract this angle covers.

The proposal has no persistent or cross-node state. It changes how llvmjit.c reads LLVM types from in-memory bitcode and adds a regression test, with no change to on-disk format, WAL, catalog, wire protocol or the extension ABI. JIT code is built per backend and never written to disk or replicated, so pg_upgrade, standbys and subscribers are not affected.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. It fixes how the JIT reads type information on AddressSanitizer test builds, adds an error check, and adds a regression test. Setting jit = on for a session is already allowed for any user, and nothing in it changes what any role can do or see.

The jit test and the 0002 check look cheap. They cost nothing for users who do not build with sanitizers or enable jit. A committer who knows the area (Andres Freund) is engaged and has already pushed 0004.
0002 and the jit test do not duplicate an existing feature closely enough to object; Andres notes in message #10 that no test forces JIT on, and he asks for a proper test.

The thread shows real demand: CI's AddressSanitizer job crashed on several patches (Row Pattern Recognition in message #11, a pageinspect JIT test in message #9), and three independent people hit it. A committer pushed 0004, and the remaining test and 0002 cost little and help everyone who runs CI.
